A1.justification: Both PDFs describe the same interaction study using SWE-Bench Verified, despite the revised title and expanded evaluation. Their text, figures, tables, equations, and appendices are readable and support reliable comparison.

before.justification: v1 reports original experiments on task resolution, ambiguity detection, navigational information, and question quality across four models.

after.justification: v2 retains those experiments, adds evaluations of two models, and reports original analyses of synthetic underspecification and alternative information-gain measurement.

M1.justification: The summarization procedure, GPT-4o user proxy, and Full/Hidden/Interaction framework remain. Although v1 already requires interaction, v2 Appendix A.7 adds a Qwen-specific clarification phase requiring questions-only output and waiting for answers before implementation. This is a limited procedural adaptation.

E1.justification: The core evaluation retains the 500 SWE-Bench Verified issues and their synthetic underspecified counterparts; naming them Ambig-SWE does not establish new coverage. Section 2.1 and Appendix A.4 add characterization of naturally underspecified SWE-Bench issues, including three examples. These broaden the analyzed population without adding agent-solving evaluations on natural underspecified issues.

E2.justification: Claude Sonnet 4 and Qwen 3 Coder 480B join the original four models in the task-resolution, detection, navigational-information, and question-quality comparisons. Their participation substantially extends the comparative evidence to stronger proprietary and open-weight models; the original comparator membership is retained.

E3.justification: The added models use OpenHands v0.60, updated prompts, and up to 100 steps, versus the original 30-turn setup. Sonnet 4's Hidden evaluation uses 100 of 500 issues, and Qwen receives additional compulsory clarification instructions. New analyses introduce summary-overlap metrics and recovery distance. These are added protocols, not evidence that the original experiments were rerun.

E4.justification: v2 adds synthetic-versus-natural issue analysis, quantitative information-loss assessment, and LLM annotations of omitted information (Section 2.1 and Appendix A.2.3). Appendix A.7 adds a Qwen trajectory case study, while Figure 7 tests an alternative recovery-distance metric. These materially expand scrutiny of dataset realism, model behavior, and measurement validity.

E5.justification: New Table 3 explicitly reports means, medians, and standard deviations for summary/full-issue comparison metrics. The Wilcoxon testing procedure and 0.05 threshold are retained, and additional model p-values do not constitute a new testing practice. Neither version reports repeated-run counts or seed-based uncertainty.

E6.justification: Original four-model resolve rates and tabulated comparisons are retained. New results include Interaction resolve rates of 46.0% for Qwen and 41.8% for Sonnet 4 (Figure 3), and detection accuracies reaching 89% for Sonnet 4 versus 50% throughout for Qwen (Table 2). Dataset-characterization and recovery-distance results are also added. These are new-model/protocol results, not same-setting improvements.

T1.justification: The Wilcoxon hypotheses and cosine-distance equation are retained across the renumbered appendices. The added recovery-distance analysis applies standard cosine distance to a different reference text; it supplies no new mathematical derivation, formal assumption, theorem, or proof.

C1.justification: The three-capability interaction thesis remains, but v2 adds a central claim that relative interaction gains diminish with increasing model capability and qualifies the earlier proprietary/open-weight contrast. The introduction and conclusion also foreground Ambig-SWE as a diagnostic benchmark and emphasize actionable clarification and adaptive information integration as principal contributions.

C2.justification: v2 explains the synthetic issues' more aggressive information removal, why natural issues lack suitable paired ground truth, and why the proxy is an information-injection mechanism rather than realistic user simulation. It adds interpretations of Qwen's rigid behavior, exploration efficiency, and recovery-distance shortcomings. These substantially extend the study's mechanisms, applicability boundaries, and measurement caveats.

D1.justification: The appendices add Docker and patch-testing details, disabled browsing, the 16-worker runtime, an omission-analysis prompt, and framework-version information for newer models. The original experimental prompts and code/data link remain. Conversely, v1's explicit list of inputs to the question-quality judge is omitted from the shortened description.

R1.justification: v2 adds references including Chen et al., Li et al., Zhong et al., and Claude 4, while removing the Rao, Pyatkin, and Kuhn clarification-question references. It sharpens the distinction between ambiguity and underspecificity and contrasts multiple interdependent information gaps with prior single-detail settings. Most of the related-work coverage remains.

P1.justification: Beyond the revised title and terminology, v2 substantially rewrites the introduction, model-family discussion, question-strategy analysis, related work, and conclusion. It replaces the introductory research-question list with contributions, merges limitations into the conclusion, reorganizes the appendices, and adds reproducibility and LLM-usage statements.

P2.justification: The main text changes from two columns to predominantly one column. Figure 3 is redrawn for six models; the original two-panel Figure 5 becomes separate Figures 5 and 6; Figure 7 and two substantive tables are added. Statistical and question-count tables move to the appendix, and the examples table is condensed and expanded. Figures 1, 2, and 4 retain their underlying artwork.

improvement.justification: v2 improves the evidence's breadth and interpretation by testing stronger models, characterizing synthetic information loss, and explaining dataset and proxy limitations. It also removes v1's contradictory statement that interaction gains were nonsignificant. The gain is bounded: different budgets and prompts complicate capability-based conclusions, and new reporting errors remain—for example, Section 5.3 claims 50% fewer questions, although Table 6's 4.03 versus 6.02 implies about 33% fewer.
